text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000215's elevated 99215 rate persists across every complexity tier, including patients with no chronic conditions, which is consistent with upcoding, but the charts returned are too few to confirm it.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The complexity table argues against a sicker-panel explanation: the 99215 share is several times the all-provider rate even for patients with 0 or 1 conditions. Sampled low-complexity 99215 claims carry minor acute or follow-up diagnoses such as upper respiratory infection or follow-up exam (C0095046, C0095258, C0094890, C0095175), and the heavy reliance on 99214 points the same way. The documentation does not confirm this, but it is too thin to judge either way: only 4 documented 99215 claims came back, all supported at high MDM (e.g., C0094596, C0094651), and one 99214 was documented low (C0095286). The 2 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed with no lab or test line on the claim are only weak evidence. Reviewers should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, including whether patient M0039833's 99215 (C0094331) and 99214 (C0095430) visits differed clinically, and check notes for cloned or templated MDM language."}
